s1_footnotes: *Representativeness of study participants is commented upon in Supplementary Table S6.

aGIST = gastrointestinal stromal tumor; LMS = leiomyosarcoma; MPNST = malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor; UPS = undifferentiated pleomotphic sarcoma. Leiomyosarcomas and myxomas were after analysis (column B) each divided into two transcriptomic subtypes (LMS Class 1 and LMS Class 2 and Myxoma Class 1 and Myxoma Class 2, respectively)

bTumor types were broadly categorized into three subgroups on the basis of presumed, typical pathogenetic mechanism: CNA = copy number aberrations,  Fusion = gene fusion, SNV = single nucleotide variants.
dTumor size (largest diameter in cm), depth (D = deep, S = superficial), and grade (according to a 3-grade scale) are indicated. NA = not available or not applicable.

eFU = follow-up in months after diagnosis, unless otherwise indicated. DoC = dead of other causes; DwD = dead with disease; DwoD = dead without disease; LR = local relapse; Met = metastasis; NED = no evidence of disease; NFUD = no followup data
fMost samples were from primary lesions but when indicated, a local recurrence (LR) or metastsis (Met) had been analyzed.
gA sample was scored as fuions-positive (Yes) if a relevant fusion was detected by RNA-seq in the present study or by other methods in previous studies.
hSilhouette (S-) scores were calculated for all tumor types represented by at least 4 samples, except for spindle cell tumors, indicated by Yes.

iCases are highlighted in yellow if the probability score was higher for another tumor type; the probability scores for the original and the suggested diagnoses are shown. Also all spindle cell tumors are highlighted in yellow, and the highest probability scores for specific diagnoses are provided. Tumors belonging to one of the three benign adipocytic tumor transcriptomic subclusters (BAT SC 1-3), intermediate and malignant tumors mapping to one of the three complex tumor transcriptomic subclusters (Complex SC1-3), and nerve sheath tumors belonging to one of the two benign nerve sheath clusters (Neurofibr SC and Schwannoma SC) are also indicated.

jSalient genomic data were derived from patient charts. Copy number profiles (CNP) derived from genomic array analysis were dichotomized into those with simple CNP (< 5 chromosomes affected) and complex CNP (>5 chromosomes affected). When only G-banding analysis had been performed, karyotypes were dichotomized into simple (<5 chromosomes affected) or complex (>5 chromosomes affected). Genomic features that are typical for certain tumor types, such as translocations causing gene fusions, deletions or amplifications, are indicated in addition to the complexity level.
kASCAT ploidy/purity estimates from tumors analyzed with SNP array and displaying copy number aberrations.

lWhen some genetic (such as karyotype) and/or clinicomorphological features of a tumor had been published before, the reference and case numbers in the Mitelman Database (MDB) of Chromosome Aberrations and Gene Fusions in Cancer (https://mitelmandatabase.isb-cgc.org/) are shown. This column also contains information on selected tumors that on the basis of their transcriptomic profile fit better with another tumor type.
mAbbreviations used in figures and supplemental files.
